extdata_file <- function(filename) {
  installed <- system.file("extdata", filename, package = "CellCharterR")

}
```

# Purpose

This is the primary CellCharterR tutorial. It starts from the official CODEX
mouse-spleen datasets, shows their `SpatialExperiment` representation, prepares
a biologically useful dominant cell-type annotation, and demonstrates the
supported downstream workflow using the independently selected **K = 4**
domains. The expensive full-data results are loaded from preserved package
artifacts, so installation and vignette rendering never rerun clustering or
the 100 sample-level permutations.

The R Torch GMM/AutoK implementation is experimental for very large datasets.
This tutorial therefore assumes that domain labels have already been computed
and stored in `colData(spe)` or a `reducedDim`. Graph construction, enrichment,
neighborhood enrichment, differential testing, and plotting remain native R
workflows.

The stored contrast is BALBc minus MRL. Rows of each matrix represent the
source or central domain, columns represent the surrounding or neighboring
domain, and arrows therefore point **source -> neighbor**. Positive effects are
shown in the BALBc panel; negative effects are displayed by absolute magnitude
in the MRL panel. Both panels reuse the same permutation p-values.

# Import the mouse-spleen data as a SpatialExperiment

The official example consists of a raw CODEX H5AD and a clustered H5AD. The
download and conversion are shown but not executed during package builds. The
second vignette gives the full checksum-verified download workflow.

```{r import-full-spe, eval=FALSE}
library(CellCharterR)

spe <- read_codex_spe(
  raw_h5ad = "data-raw/codex-mouse-spleen/codex_mouse_spleen.h5ad",
  clustered_h5ad = "data-raw/codex-mouse-spleen/codex_mouse_spleen_clustered.h5ad",
  representation_dataset = "obsm/X_trVAE",
  spatial_dataset = "obsm/spatial"
)
```

The converted full object contains 707,474 segmented cells. Protein expression
and the supplied trVAE representation can remain disk-backed, whereas spatial
coordinates use the native `spatialCoords()` slot.

```{r inspect-full-spe, eval=FALSE}
spe
dim(spe)
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(spe)
colnames(SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe))
SingleCellExperiment::reducedDimNames(spe)
SpatialExperiment::spatialCoordsNames(spe)
SingleCellExperiment::colPairNames(spe)
```

After the graph and precomputed domain labels are added, the recommended object
organization is:

```text
class: SpatialExperiment
dimensions: 29 proteins × 707,474 segmented cells
assays: protein (disk-backed)
spatialCoords: spatial (x, y)
reducedDims: X_trVAE, X_cellcharter
colData: sample, condition, cell_type, dominant_cell_type,
         cellcharter_domain_k4
colPairs: cellcharter_graph
metadata: CellCharterR results and provenance
```

The domain labels do not require a special registration function. Downstream
functions read `domain_col` directly from `colData`, a one-column `reducedDim`,
or an unambiguous named column inside a `reducedDim`.

# Assign a dominant cell type

The CODEX H5AD already contains a detailed per-cell annotation. For readable
domain enrichment, closely related dendritic, stromal, and residual labels are
collapsed into a dominant cell-type variable. This is an annotation step, not
a CellCharter clustering step.

```{r dominant-cell-type, eval=FALSE}
dominant_cell_type <- as.character(spe$cell_type)

collapsed <- c(
  "CD4(+)CD8(-)cDC" = "DCs",
  "CD4(-)CD8(+)cDC" = "DCs",
  "CD4(-)CD8(-) cDC" = "DCs",
  "CD106(+)CD16/32(+)CD31(+) stroma" = "stroma",
  "CD106(+)CD16/32(+)CD31(-)Ly6C(-) stroma" = "stroma",
  "CD106(-)CD16/32(-)Ly6C(+)CD31(+) stroma" = "stroma",
  "ERTR7(+) stroma" = "stroma",
  "CD3(+) other markers (-)" = "other",
  "CD106(+)CD16/32(-)Ly6C(+)CD31(+)" = "other",
  "CD106(-)CD16/32(+)Ly6C(+)CD31(-)" = "other",
  "noid" = "other",
  "CD4(+)MHCII(+)" = "other",
  "capsule" = "other"
)

replacement <- unname(collapsed[dominant_cell_type])
dominant_cell_type[!is.na(replacement)] <- replacement[!is.na(replacement)]
spe$dominant_cell_type <- factor(dominant_cell_type)
table(spe$dominant_cell_type)
```

# Build or reuse the spatial graph

If the SPE does not already contain the graph, build a sample-local Delaunay
graph from native spatial coordinates. Long links are trimmed automatically;
physical samples are never connected to one another.

```{r build-graph, eval=FALSE}
spe <- cellcharter_graph(
  spe,
  spatial = "spatial",
  sample_col = "sample",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph"
)

SingleCellExperiment::colPairNames(spe)
SingleCellExperiment::colPair(spe, "cellcharter_graph")
```

# Load the preserved downstream results

```{r load-result}
library(CellCharterR)

k4_result <- readRDS(extdata_file("mouse_spleen_k4_diff_nhood.rds"))

k4_enrichment <- readRDS(extdata_file("mouse_spleen_k4_enrichment.rds"))

k4_result$params[c(
  "contrast_definition", "library_unit", "library_counts",
  "n_perms", "permutation_mode", "empirical_tail"
)]
```

This result compares three BALBc libraries with six MRL libraries, uses the
sample as the permutation unit, and contains 100 permutations with the pinned
CellCharter 0.2.0 compatibility mode. Its SHA-256 checksum is
`ae65446954faeb1b15aa53bcf5f1ec45e2ebd09d553a61a12c59c28029c3f6d7`.
The matching cell-type enrichment artifact has SHA-256 checksum
`be78548f33e16fd2f668c79cd7aa539a97df95f4a9a7ccdd0ab1b00665c0d261`.

# Compute cell-type enrichment

With dominant cell types and precomputed K=4 domains in the SPE, the complete
computation is one call. This code is shown but not rerun here; the following
figure loads its preserved result.

```{r compute-enrichment, eval=FALSE}
spe <- cellcharter_enrichment(
  spe,
  group_col = "dominant_cell_type",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain_k4",
  result_name = "cell_type_enrichment",
  log2_fold_change = TRUE
)
```

## Meet the spatial ecosystems

Before interpreting connections between domains, first inspect which cell types
characterize each domain. The dot plot shows positive observed-to-expected
cell-type enrichment as log2 fold change. Darker and larger red points indicate
stronger positive enrichment; non-positive values remain in the stored result
but are omitted from this display, following the CellCharter presentation.

```{r ecosystem-enrichment, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Cell-type enrichment defining the four K=4 mouse-spleen spatial ecosystems.", fig.alt="Positive cell-type enrichment dot plot defining four K equals 4 mouse-spleen spatial ecosystems"}
cellcharter_plot_enrichment(
  k4_enrichment,
  title = "Cell types defining the K=4 spatial ecosystems"
)
```

These enrichment profiles provide the biological context for the numbered
nodes below: each network node is one of these four spatial ecosystems, not an
individual cell type.

# Spatial-neighborhood enrichment in healthy and lupus spleen

The differential result retains the complete observed, expected, and
observed-minus-expected matrices for BALBc and MRL. The heatmaps below show the
condition-specific directed neighborhood enrichment before taking their
contrast. Rows are central ecosystems and columns are their neighbors.

```{r condition-neighborhood-heatmaps, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.8, fig.cap="Directed K=4 spatial-neighborhood enrichment in healthy BALBc and lupus MRL mouse spleen.", fig.alt="Side-by-side heatmaps of directed spatial neighborhood enrichment in BALBc and MRL mouse spleen"}
neighborhood_long <- function(x, condition) {
  value <- as.data.frame(as.table(x), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(value) <- c("source", "target", "enrichment")
  value$condition <- condition
  value$label <- ifelse(is.finite(value$enrichment), sprintf("%.2f", value$enrichment), "")
  value
}

condition_neighborhood <- rbind(
  neighborhood_long(k4_result$enrichment$BALBc, "Healthy — BALBc"),
  neighborhood_long(k4_result$enrichment$MRL, "Lupus — MRL")
)
neighborhood_limit <- max(abs(condition_neighborhood$enrichment), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  condition_neighborhood,
  ggplot2::aes(x = target, y = source, fill = enrichment)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = label), size = 5) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~condition, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#8B0000",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-neighborhood_limit, neighborhood_limit),
    name = "Observed −\nexpected"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Neighboring ecosystem (target)",
    y = "Central ecosystem (source)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

The corresponding full computation uses the graph, domain labels, biological
condition, and sample/library identifiers. Sample is the permutation unit.

```{r compute-differential, eval=FALSE}
spe <- cellcharter_diff_nhood_enrichment(
  spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain_k4",
  condition_col = "condition",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  permutation_mode = "cellcharter_v0.2.0",
  result_name = "BALBc_vs_MRL"
)
```

# Inspect both differential contrasts

Before reducing the result to arrows, inspect the complete directed effect
matrices. The stored effect is BALBc minus MRL; the reciprocal display negates
that effect while retaining the same directional empirical p-values. Rows are
source ecosystems and columns are neighboring target ecosystems. A star marks
an empirical `p <= 0.05` from the 100 sample-level permutations.

```{r contrast-heatmaps, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.8, fig.cap="Full K=4 differential neighborhood-enrichment matrices in both display directions.", fig.alt="Side-by-side heatmaps of the BALBc minus MRL and MRL minus BALBc differential neighborhood enrichment matrices"}
contrast_long <- function(effect, pvalue, contrast) {
  value <- as.data.frame(as.table(effect), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(value) <- c("source", "target", "effect")
  value$pvalue <- as.vector(pvalue)
  value$contrast <- contrast
  value$label <- ifelse(
    is.finite(value$effect),
    paste0(sprintf("%.2f", value$effect), ifelse(value$pvalue <= 0.05, " *", "")),
    ""
  )
  value
}

contrast_heatmaps <- rbind(
  contrast_long(k4_result$effect, k4_result$pvalue, "BALBc minus MRL"),
  contrast_long(-k4_result$effect, k4_result$pvalue, "MRL minus BALBc")
)
effect_limit <- max(abs(contrast_heatmaps$effect), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  contrast_heatmaps,
  ggplot2::aes(x = target, y = source, fill = effect)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = label), size = 5) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~contrast, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#8B0000",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-effect_limit, effect_limit),
    name = "Differential\nenrichment"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Neighboring ecosystem (target)",
    y = "Central ecosystem (source)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

These heatmaps retain every directed off-diagonal comparison, including weak
or unsupported effects. The network views below summarize the same matrices;
they do not perform a second statistical test.

# Plot the differential graph

Black arrows are the default. Solid arrows pass the displayed statistical
threshold; dashed arrows are retained effects that are not statistically
supported at that threshold. Arrow width is intentionally constant, so it does
not create an additional visual claim about magnitude.

```{r default-network, fig.cap="Full mouse-spleen K=4 differential neighborhood-enrichment network. The two panels share identical node coordinates.", fig.alt="Two-panel K equals 4 differential neighborhood network showing both condition contrast directions with shared node positions"}
cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(k4_result)
```

The graph is asymmetric: domain 0 -> domain 2 and domain 2 -> domain 0 are
different directed hypotheses. Their effects and p-values must not be combined
or interpreted as an undirected connection.

# Apply user-defined condition colors

Colors are presentation choices, not part of the statistical test. A single
color applies to both panels; a named vector can assign one color per condition.

```{r custom-colours, fig.cap="The same result with user-supplied condition colors and the strongest four arrows retained independently per panel.", fig.alt="Differential neighborhood network with dark blue and dark red condition colors and four strongest arrows per panel"}
cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(
  k4_result,
  edge_colours = c(BALBc = "#2166AC", MRL = "#B2182B"),
  top_n = 4
)
```

`top_n` is a display filter. It is applied independently in each panel after
p-values have been evaluated and therefore does not alter the p-values or their
multiple-testing adjustment.

# Focus on statistically supported arrows

The reference-compatible default uses raw directional empirical p-values.
For exploratory multiplicity control, select a method supported by
`stats::p.adjust()`; adjustment is performed across every eligible directed
off-diagonal hypothesis before display filtering.

```{r supported-only, fig.cap="Edges supported by the raw directional empirical p-value threshold of 0.05.", fig.alt="Differential neighborhood network restricted to edges with raw directional empirical p values no greater than 0.05"}
cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(
  k4_result,
  significant_only = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05
)
```

# Illustrative interpretation

In this K = 4 result, the largest positive displayed effect is the directed
association from domain 1 to domain 2, favoring BALBc. At the raw threshold of
0.05, three BALBc-favored arrows are retained and no MRL-favored arrow passes
the same threshold. A recorded p-value of zero means that none of the 100
reference-compatible permutation draws was as extreme; it does **not** mean
that the probability is literally zero.

These domain numbers do not themselves identify cell types or mechanisms.
Biological interpretation should combine this network with the corresponding
spatial maps, cell-type enrichment results, sample-level consistency, and the
known limitations of the K = 4 domain resolution. The figure is therefore a
diagnostic summary of the computed differential neighborhood result, not proof
of a causal interaction.

# Reproduce the downstream analysis

The following code documents where the plotted differential result originates,
but it is not run when the vignette is built. It starts from the full SPE with
precomputed domains; it does not invoke R Torch GMM or AutoK.

```{r reproduce-result, eval=FALSE}
spe <- cellcharter_diff_nhood_enrichment(
  spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain_k4",
  condition_col = "condition",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  permutation_mode = "cellcharter_v0.2.0",
  result_name = "BALBc_vs_MRL"
)

cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(spe, result_name = "BALBc_vs_MRL")
```
